hypotheses.title: Competitor Return Spread Regime with Operational Cashflow Efficiency Leverage Boost
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Information from peer competitor revaluation (pv13, rel_ret_comp) diffuses gradually across equities sharing identical supplier costs and customer demand. Evaluating when the 10-day decayed competitor spread (rel_ret_comp - (close - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)) is above median (rank > 0.5) identifies equities poised for catch-up revaluation. When in this regime, applying a +1 leverage boost to square-root compressed operational cash generation derivative (cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative in model16, 100% coverage) concentrates capital into high-quality companies experiencing peer revaluation. Subindustry neutralization isolates firm-specific turnaround with zero overlap to news models, guaranteeing self-correlation < 0.35.
confounders: Sudden sector-wide multiple compression that overrides operational cashflow improvements
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if competitor regime cashflow boost yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Ternary leverage boost applying +1 to operational cashflow efficiency derivative when 10-day decayed competitor lead-lag spread exceeds median.

hypotheses.title: Cashflow Efficiency Acceleration Regime with Competitor Lead-Lag Revaluation Boost
hypotheses.economic_rationale: cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative (model16, 100% matrix coverage in TOP3000) measures daily acceleration in operational profitability per unit of capital. When its 40-day cumulative sum is above median (rank > 0.5), the equity operates in a persistent fundamental turnaround regime. Applying a +1 leverage boost to the compressed competitor lead-lag return spread (power(rank(rel_ret_comp - (close - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)), 0.5)) allocates capital to equities whose peers have rallied but whose own prices have lagged, backed by audited operational turnaround. 100% coverage across TOP3000, zero analyst or news overlap, ensuring self-correlation < 0.35.
confounders: Supply-chain disruptions that temporarily bottleneck cash conversion despite peer order growth
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cashflow regime competitor boost yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.expression: rank(ts_sum(cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative, 40)) > 0.5 ? power(rank(rel_ret_comp - (close - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)), 0.5) + 1 : power(rank(rel_ret_comp - (close - ts_delay(close, 1)) / ts_delay(close, 1)), 0.5)
candidates.rationale: Ternary leverage boost applying +1 to competitor lead-lag return spread when 40-day cumulative cashflow efficiency derivative is above median.

hypotheses.title: Direct Competitor Lead-Lag Return Spread with 10-Day Smoothing and Decay 8 Optimization
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In Batch 305 Candidate 1, the 60-day rolling rank of direct competitor spread delivered Sharpe 1.70, Sub-universe Sharpe 1.56, and zero correlation, but turnover at 45.45% under Decay 4 kept Fitness at 0.86. Extending the internal linear decay from 5 to 10 days and pairing with simulator Decay 8 slashes turnover by ~50% into the optimal 18%-22% corridor. Because Fitness scales inversely with the square root of turnover, this halving of rebalancing churn directly pushes Fitness from 0.86 to > 1.20, achieving a full 8 PASS clean slate on an untouched pv13 dataset.
confounders: Macroeconomic factor rotation that causes prolonged divergence between competitor baskets
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if smoothed competitor spread yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 10-day linear decay of 60-day rolling time-series rank of direct competitor return spread over equity returns.
